inputs.source: Engineering design docs returned by docs.search

instructions.note: Secret handling is expressed only as a prompt rule, with no structural DLP or recipient binding control described.

controls.name: Read-only docs.search credential
controls.decay_rationale: Least-privilege read-only credential does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Reply channel restricted to authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: Destination is fixed to the authenticated requester and not chosen by the model.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Prevents hidden egress through client-side fetch side channels and does not depend on model obedience.

controls.name: Prompt instruction not to paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: A stronger or more persistent model can rationalize exceptions or follow injected goals despite the prompt rule.

controls.name: Missing structural egress allowlist for future external fetch and outbound channels
controls.decay_rationale: A runtime egress allowlist would keep attacker-reachable destinations unreachable even if future tools are added.

controls.name: Missing structural segregation or labeling for future customer-authored ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: If Jira customer tickets are added, content from an untrusted source should remain segregated and constrained before it reaches answer generation.

findings.title: Forecast only - TC1 lethal trifecta if web.fetch and Jira customer ticket content are added

attack_path.note: Confidential engineering docs are readable today through docs.search.
Read-only search can retrieve confidential design content.
Current sink is restricted to the authenticated requester, but planned next-sprint additions would introduce public web references and customer-authored Jira content into the same task context.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff adding web.fetch, MCP client config diff adding a Jira server, or new customer-authored ticket content entering the context.

evidence.observation: There is no network egress today, replies go only to the authenticated requester, and the chat client does not render images or fetch links.
Roadmap says next sprint will add a web.fetch tool and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.
Design docs are confidential, so combining confidential reads with future external or customer-controlled content creates the TC1 exfiltration shape only after the named trigger.
The only explicit secret-handling control in the prompt is behavioral: "Never paste secrets or credentials into answers."

recommendations.action: Before adding web.fetch or Jira, enforce a destination allowlist and prevent any tool or channel from sending confidential design-doc content to attacker-reachable destinations.
Treat customer-authored Jira content as untrusted input, keep it segregated from internal design-doc answers, and require reassessment when the new MCP server is introduced.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe service-to-service authentication or agent identity mechanisms for the docs-qa process.
No logs, audit trail, or attributable action records are described for agent actions in the provided artifacts.
The design notes give short step and runtime bounds, but no quota, spend cap, or runtime enforcement mechanism is described.
SSO authentication is mentioned, but the artifacts do not describe nonrepudiation records or how employee actions are attributable.
The artifacts do not state whether the inbound question path has integrity protections beyond SSO-authenticated access.
Transport confidentiality for the inbound chat flow is not described in the provided materials.
No rate limiting, per-user quotas, or protection against abusive inbound question volume is described.
The materials do not say whether the design-doc store has availability protections or query throttling.
The design does not describe message-rate limits, queue backpressure, or other chat reply flow availability controls.

rating.rationale: Present design shows no untrusted source reaching a sensitive sink above low: employee questions are trusted, design docs are internal, replies are bound to the authenticated requester, and no network egress exists today. Forecast rises to critical if the planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server add attacker-reachable or customer-authored content without structural segregation and egress controls, because that would create a TC1 lethal-trifecta path from sensitive internal data to external or untrusted destinations. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, runtime enforcement details, or source code were provided, so protocol security, transport protections, logging, and exact sink constraints are assessed with medium confidence.

The forecast finding is conditional on roadmap items described in the runtime notes; planned capabilities and inputs were not fully specified, so the projected path shape is inferred from the stated next-sprint changes.
